A1.justification: Both complete 61-page PDFs describe the same translation-head study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices can be matched, including material relocated between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original activation-patching, translation-steering, ablation, and representation-analysis results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional cross-direction cosine-similarity comparisons in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The corruption schemes, KL-based token selection, activation-patching procedure, averaged steering vectors, and inference-time interventions remain unchanged. The revised representation analysis does not alter the translation method.

E1.justification: Both versions use FLORES-200 with the same 20 English-centered translation directions. FineWebEdu already supplies the 1,000-sample control in v1 Appendix C.2; its appearance in v2 Section 5 adds no dataset or task.

E2.justification: The instructed zero-shot and few-shot comparisons, random-head ablation controls, alternative token-selection strategies, and FineWebEdu representation baseline are retained. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The auxiliary similarity-comparison design expands from separate groups of ten English-source and ten English-target directions in v1 Figure 70 to joint comparisons across all 20 directions in v2 Figure 6. FLORES splits, model configurations, decoding settings, and the 1,000-sample control remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The geometric transferability analysis adds comparisons between English-source and English-target directions. Existing head ablations, shot-count and amplification-factor studies, token-position comparisons, and qualitative failure cases are retained. The decoding tables are relocated or repeated, not new analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; averaging and the 1,000-sample random control already appear in v1.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds cross-group similarity entries while retaining the previously plotted within-group values. Section 5 changes the similarity summary from generally above 0.9 to generally 0.7–0.9 for the expanded comparison. Section 6 changes the unrecovered Zhang et al. head identifier from [30, 18] to [31, 8]. Translation benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The activation-patching delta, KL-based selection rule, and prompt-construction definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of sparse, largely separable language and translation heads, effective steering of approximately 1% of each group, and transferable equivalence vectors.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets the existing FineWebEdu control as addressing anisotropy and head-level artifacts. It elaborates language-vector similarities through named script or linguistic-proximity examples, including Japanese–Chinese and Portuguese–Spanish. The Wolof limitation and overall transferability interpretation were already present.

D1.justification: V1 Appendix C.2 specifies a randomly selected token index for the FineWebEdu control; the replacement discussion in v2 Section 5 omits this detail. Code and resource links, prompt construction, and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Anonymous (2025) becomes Liu et al. (2026), with an updated title and publication information but the same identifying reference URL. This is the same cited work, and its relationship to the present study is unchanged. No other cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: V2 prefixes the title with 'Translation Heads', updates publication information and acknowledgments, and rewrites the geometric discussion in Section 5. Appendix C.3 becomes B.6, while C.2 is incorporated into the main discussion. Most prose and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V1 Figure 70's four annotated similarity panels become two compact joint-direction panels in v2 Figure 6, without numerical cell annotations. V1 Table 7 is repeated as v2 Table 1 and retained as Table 8. Other figures and appendix tables are principally relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The expanded similarity comparisons and integration of existing decoding evidence into Section 5 modestly strengthen the presentation of transferability. Changing the unrecovered head identifier also resolves v1's contradictory classification of [30, 18]. These limited gains are tempered by smaller, unannotated similarity plots and omission of the random-token-index detail; the central method and translation-performance evidence remain unchanged.
